newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine police end jobless siege with tear gas.
newsitem.headline: Argentine police end jobless siege with tear gas.

text.p: Seven people were injured on Friday when Argentine police used tear gas and rubber bullets to end a siege of a town hall by 300 jobless protesters in the Patagonian province of Neuquen.
Police launched a raid before dawn and angry protestors set fire to the mayor's car in the town of Cutral Co, local news agencies and television reported.
Demonstrators began besieging Cutral Co town hall Thursday to demand higher unemployment benefits, trapping the deputy governor of Neuquen and other senior provincial officials.

The incidents ended a brief calm in Cutral Co, where unemployed protestors clashed violently with the police two months ago, beginning a wave of unrest and roadblock protests that spread to the provinces of Jujuy, Salta and Cordoba.
The national government was forced to promise aid to Jujuy to help foster the creation of 10,000 jobs and end a long roadblock there by thousands of protesters in late May.
Argentina's unemployment rate has soared under the government of President Carlos Menem to 17.3 percent, and is much worse in many of the poorer provinces.
The government is hoping that renewed economic growth and a plan to make labour conditions more flexible will eventually cut into the jobless rate.
